name: Question 16
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/ca49b92d602d04a73dc7ab9936d601654bd293ce3fb7950372ac86155875aca3.png)

Evaluate the triple integral 
${∭}_{R}\frac{1}{6-y+3z}\,dV$
over the region $R,$ shown above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the front one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/0008ba406cfe8a5b61d683a6854260897cb441752a5333add281ab1279e31b0b.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 2-\frac{y}{3}+z},
$$

where

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,\,0\le z\le 3}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/bbe6b6b897e5d53421080ae8e8b9dc49f2ea1b7e135f8426ee3f11af01cc2401.png)

Hence, we can express the region $R$ as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,\,0\le z\le 3,\,\,0\le 2-\frac{y}{3}+z}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{6-y+3z}\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-y/3+z}\frac{1}{6-y+3z}\,dx\,dz\,dy.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x$, treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2-y/3+z}\frac{1}{6-y+3z}\,dx\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{0}^{2-y/3+z}\frac{1}{6-y+3z}\,dx]dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{6-y+3z}[x]_{x=0}^{x=2-y/3+z}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{6-y+3z}(2-\frac{y}{3}+z)\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{3}\,dz\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{3}\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{3}\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{3}{[z]}_{z=0}^{z=3}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{3}(3)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}\,dy & =[y]_{y=0}^{y=3} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

R={(x,y,z):(y,z)∈D,0≤x≤2−y3+z},

where

D={(y,z):0≤y≤3,0≤z≤3}

is the projection of R onto the yz-plane, shown below.

Hence, we can express the region R as

R={(x,y,z):0≤y≤3,0≤z≤3,0≤2−y3+z}

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

∭R16−y+3zdV=∫03∫03∫02−y/3+z16−y+3zdxdzdy.

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to x, treating y and z as constants:

∫03∫03∫02−y/3+z16−y+3zdxdzdy=∫03∫03[∫02−y/3+z16−y+3zdx]dzdy=∫03∫0316−y+3z[x]x=0x=2−y/3+zdzdy=∫03∫0316−y+3z(2−y3+z)dzdy=∫03∫0313dzdy

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to z, treating y as a constant:

∫03∫0313dzdy=∫03[∫0313dz]dy=∫0313[z]z=0z=3dy=∫0313(3)dy=∫03dy

Finally, we integrate with respect to y:

∫03dy=[y]y=0y=3=3.
